subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4
solution:
The correct answer is '**eye**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence refers to makeup artists and cameramen being responsible for the visual appearance of the heroine.
 
• The correct idiom is “keep a careful eye on,” which means to watch or monitor closely.
 
• "**Eye**" fits both idiomatically and contextually, as it's about visual attention.
 
• Other options like "**nose**", "**ear**", and "**leg**" do not make sense in this context or follow any known idiomatic usage relevant here.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Passage: *Until that moment, every director in Hollywood had accepted as gospel * *truth__* * that the audience should not be taxed too much. Welles struck a * *__blow__* * at these beliefs, without displaying the slightest of qualms. Visually, 'Citizen Kane' was shot with a harsh sharpness which * *__permeated__* * every scene. Traditionally, every make-up man and cameraman in Hollywood had to keep a careful * *__eye__* * on the appearance of the heroine. Welles refused to follow this **_________****in the case of his own heroine. For the first time, dialogue was presented in its realistic form.* 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Nose: No idiom or contextual meaning fits with “keep a careful nose on.”
 
• Ear: Typically used in the context of listening, not watching appearances.
 
• Leg: Irrelevant in this context and grammatically incorrect.
